title.zh: 卷九十二 列傳第五十二 良吏
title.raw: 卷九十二 列傳第五十二 良吏 Volume 92 Biographies 52: Liang Li

sentences.zh: 列傳第五十二 良吏

translations.literal: Biographies 52: Good Officials
translations.idiomatic: Biography 52: Good Officials

sentences.zh: 高祖起自匹庶，知民事艱難，及登庸作宰，留心吏職，而王略外舉，未遑內務。

translations.literal: The Founder Emperor rose from common status, knew the hardships of the people's affairs, and when he took office as chief minister paid attention to the duties of officials; yet his royal strategy was raised outward, and he had no leisure for internal affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu arose from humble ranks and understood how hard ordinary life could be. Once he held high office as chief minister, he kept an eye on the duties of local administrators; but with his royal strategy turned outward, he had little room left for domestic administration.

sentences.zh: 奉師之費，日耗千金，播茲寬簡，雖所未暇，而絀華屏欲，以儉抑身，左右無幸謁之私，閨房無文綺之飾，故能戎車歲駕，邦甸不憂。

translations.literal: The expense of supporting the army daily consumed a thousand in gold; to spread such leniency and simplicity, though what he had no time for, he reined in extravagance and restrained desire, used frugality to check himself, his attendants had no private privilege of favored petition, and his inner quarters had no ornament of patterned silk; therefore he could drive the war chariot year after year, and the realm's domains were not worried.
translations.idiomatic: Campaign costs ran to a thousand gold a day, so he had no chance to put his lenient, simple policies fully into practice; still he cut back splendor and checked his appetites, living thriftily himself, forbidding favoritism among attendants and luxuries in the inner apartments—so year after year the armies went to war without plunging the realm into distress.

sentences.zh: 太祖幼而寬仁，入纂大業，及難興陝方，六戎薄伐，命將動師，經略司、兗，費由府實，役不及民。

translations.literal: The Founding Emperor was from youth broad and benevolent; he entered to succeed the great enterprise, and when difficulties arose in the Shaan region and the six Rong pressed in attack, he ordered generals to move troops, planned strategy in Si and Yan provinces, expenses came from the treasury's substance, and corvée labor did not reach the people.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizu had been gentle and generous since youth. After he took over the great enterprise, when troubles flared in the Shaan region and the northern tribes pressed the borders, he sent generals to campaign in the Si and Yan circuit; costs were borne by the treasury, and the people were not pressed into labor.

sentences.zh: 自此區宇宴安，方內無事，三十年間，氓庶蕃息，奉上供徭，止於歲賦，晨出莫歸，自事而已。

translations.literal: From this the realm was peaceful and secure, within the four directions there was no trouble; for thirty years the common people multiplied, serving the court with tribute and corvée only to the annual tax levy, going out at dawn and returning at dusk, attending to their own affairs alone.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the realm lay at peace and the interior knew no disturbance. For thirty years the common people flourished; what they owed the court was limited to the annual tax. They left at dawn, returned at dusk, and minded their own affairs.

sentences.zh: 守宰之職，以六期為斷，雖沒世不徙，未及曩時，而民有所係，吏無苟得。

translations.literal: The duties of prefects and magistrates were fixed at six-year terms; though they might not be transferred for a lifetime, it did not reach former times, yet the people had something to rely on and officials had no careless gain.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects and magistrates served six-year terms. Though some held office for life without transfer—a practice not as strict as in earlier times—the people still had officials they could depend on, and clerks could not grab gains at will.

sentences.zh: 家給人足，即事雖難，轉死溝渠，于時可免。

translations.literal: Households had provision and people had sufficiency; even if affairs were difficult, turning dead in ditches and channels, at that time it could be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: Households were supplied and people had enough. Even when times were hard, the starving dead in ditches and canals—a scourge that could then be avoided.

sentences.zh: 凡百戶之鄉，有市之邑，歌謠舞蹈，觸處成群，蓋宋世之極盛也。

translations.literal: In every village of a hundred households, in every market town, songs and dances, wherever touched formed groups—this was roughly the utmost prosperity of the Song age.
translations.idiomatic: In hamlets of a hundred households and in market towns, song and dance broke out everywhere in groups—such was the height of Song prosperity.

sentences.zh: 暨元嘉二十七年，北狄南侵，戎役大起，傾資掃蓄，猶有未供，於是深賦厚斂，天下騷動。

translations.literal: When it came to the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia, the northern Di invaded south, military service greatly arose, pouring out funds and sweeping stores yet still having what was not supplied; thereupon deep taxes and heavy levies—the realm was in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: By the twenty-seventh year of Yuanjia, northern enemies invaded from the south and military service surged. Treasuries and stores were emptied and still could not meet demand; heavy taxes followed, and the realm was thrown into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 自茲至於孝建，兵連不息，以區區之江東，地方不至數千里，戶不盈百萬，薦之以師旅，因之以凶荒，宋氏之盛，自此衰矣。

translations.literal: From this until Xiaojian, warfare was unceasing; with the mere Jiangdong region, territory not reaching several thousand li, households not filling a million, heaped upon with armies, compounded with famine and disaster—the Song clan's prosperity from this declined.
translations.idiomatic: From then until the Xiaojian era, war never ceased. In the small Jiangdong domain—less than a few thousand li across, with fewer than a million households—armies and famine piled on one another, and Song greatness began to wane.

sentences.zh: 晉世諸帝，多處內房，朝宴所臨，東西二堂而已。

translations.literal: The emperors of the Jin age mostly dwelt in inner chambers; for morning feasts they attended only the eastern and western halls.
translations.idiomatic: Jin emperors mostly stayed within the inner quarters; for court banquets they used only the eastern and western halls.

sentences.zh: 孝武末年，清暑方構，高祖受命，無所改作，所居唯稱西殿，不制嘉名；

translations.literal: In the last years of Emperor Xiaowu, the Clear Summer [pavilion] was just being built; when the Founder Emperor received the Mandate, he made no alterations; where he dwelt was only called the Western Hall, without devising an elegant name;
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Xiaowu's last years the Clear Summer Pavilion was under construction. When Gaozu took the throne he changed nothing: his residence was simply called the Western Hall, without a grand ceremonial name;

sentences.zh: 太祖因之，亦有合殿之稱。

translations.literal: the Founding Emperor followed this, and also had the name of the United Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu followed suit and also used the name United Hall.

sentences.zh: 及世祖承統，制度奢廣，犬馬餘菽粟，土木衣綈繡，追陋前規，更造正光、玉燭、紫極諸殿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu succeeded to the succession, institutions were extravagant and broad; dogs and horses had surplus grain, earth and wood wore silk gauze, pursuing what was mean in former regulations, he newly built the Zhengguang, Yuzhu, and Ziji halls and others.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu came to the throne, institutions grew lavish and vast: dogs and horses had grain to spare, builders dressed timber in silk brocade. Casting aside the frugal precedents, he erected the Zhengguang, Yuzhu, Ziji, and other halls anew.

sentences.zh: 雕欒綺節，珠窗網戶，嬖女幸臣，賜傾府藏，竭四海不供其欲，單民命未快其心。

translations.literal: Carved beams with brocade ornament, pearl windows and net doors, favored women and favored ministers—gifts emptied the treasury stores; exhausting the four seas could not supply their desires, and the lone commoner's life did not please their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Carved beams bore brocade tracery; pearl windows and latticed doors gleamed. Favored women and court favorites drew gifts that drained the treasury; all within the four seas could not satisfy their wants, and a single commoner's life was not enough to please them.

sentences.zh: 太宗繼阼，彌篤浮侈，恩不恤下，以至橫流。

translations.literal: Emperor Taizong succeeded to the throne, even more earnest in floating extravagance, grace not caring for those below, reaching to overflowing current.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong succeeded him and pursued extravagance all the more, showing no concern for those below until abuses overflowed everywhere.

sentences.zh: 蒞民之官，遷變歲屬，灶不得黔，席未暇暖，蒲、密之化，事未易階。

translations.literal: Officials who presided over the people changed year by year; the stove could not turn black, the mat had no time to warm—transformations like those of Pu and Mi were affairs not easy to ascend to.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates who governed the people were rotated every year: the stove never blackened, the mat never warmed. The civilizing reforms of Pu and Mi were not something one could reach in a single step.

sentences.zh: 豈徒吏不及古，民偽于昔，蓋由為上所擾，致治莫從。

translations.literal: How could it be only that officials did not reach antiquity and the people were false compared with the past? It was fundamentally because they were disturbed by what was above, so that achieving order had nothing to follow.
translations.idiomatic: It was not merely that officials fell short of antiquity or the people grew more deceitful than before; the rulers above kept disrupting them, so good government had no chance to take hold.

sentences.zh: 今采其風跡粗著者，以為《良吏篇》云。

translations.literal: Now I gather those whose conduct and traces are roughly notable, to make the 'Good Officials' chapter.
translations.idiomatic: Here I collect those whose reputations stand out clearly enough to form this chapter on Good Officials.

sentences.zh: 王鎮之，字伯重，琅邪臨沂人，征士弘之兄也。

translations.literal: Wang Zhenzhi, style name Bozhong, was a man of Linyi in Langye, elder brother of the recluse Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhenzhi, courtesy name Bozhong, came from Linyi in Langye and was the elder brother of the recluse Wang Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 曾祖暠，晉驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Hao was Jin General of Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Wang Hao served Jin as General of Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 祖耆之，中書郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qizhi was Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wang Qizhi was a Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 父隨之，上虞令。

translations.literal: His father Suizhi was magistrate of Shangyu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Suizhi was magistrate of Shangyu.

sentences.zh: 鎮之初為琅邪王衛軍行參軍，出補剡、上虞令，並有能名。

translations.literal: Zhenzhi at first was Acting Army Aide to the Prince of Langye's Guard General; going out he filled posts as magistrate of Shan and Shangyu, both with reputations for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzhi first served as acting aide in the guard of the Prince of Langye, then took outside appointments as magistrate of Shan and Shangyu, winning a name for competence in both posts.

sentences.zh: 內史謝輶請為山陰令，復有殊績。

translations.literal: Interior Minister Xie Zhou requested him as magistrate of Shanyin, and again he had outstanding achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Interior Minister Xie Zhou asked that he be made magistrate of Shanyin, where he again produced exceptional results.

sentences.zh: 遷衛軍參軍，本國郎中令，加寧朔將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Army Aide of the Guard General, Grandee Master of the Original State, with additional title General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to army aide of the guard general, grandee master of his native commandery, and additionally made General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 桓玄輔晉，以為大將軍錄事參軍。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan assisted Jin, he was made Chief Clerk Aide to the Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan dominated Jin, Zhenzhi was appointed chief clerk aide to the grand general.

sentences.zh: 時三吳饑荒，遣鎮之銜命賑恤，而會稽內史王愉不奉符旨，鎮之依事糾奏。

translations.literal: At that time the Three Wu region had famine; they sent Zhenzhi bearing orders to relieve and succor, but Kuaiji Interior Minister Wang Yu did not follow the talisman edict; Zhenzhi according to the matter impeached and memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck the Three Wu region, Zhenzhi was sent with imperial orders to provide relief. Kuaiji interior minister Wang Yu refused to obey the edict, and Zhenzhi impeached him on the facts.

sentences.zh: 愉子綏，玄之外甥，當時貴盛，鎮之為所排抑，以母老求補安成太守。

translations.literal: Yu had a son Sui, Huan Xuan's nephew by a sister, at the time noble and flourishing; Zhenzhi was by him pushed down and suppressed, and because his mother was old requested appointment as supplemental prefect of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu's son Sui was Huan Xuan's nephew and then at the height of power; Zhenzhi was sidelined by them and, citing his mother's age, asked to be made prefect of Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 及玄敗，玄將苻宏寇亂郡境，鎮之拒戰彌年，子弟五人，並臨陣見殺。

translations.literal: When Xuan was defeated, Xuan's general Fu Hong raided and disturbed the commandery borders; Zhenzhi resisted in battle for a full year; five sons and younger brothers all faced the battle line and were killed.
translations.idiomatic: After Huan Xuan's fall, his general Fu Hong ravaged the commandery. Zhenzhi held out in battle for a year; five of his sons and younger brothers were killed in action.

sentences.zh: 母憂去職，在官清潔，妻子無以自給，乃棄家致喪還上虞舊基。

translations.literal: On his mother's mourning he left office; in office he was pure and clean, wife and children had no means to support themselves, so he abandoned the household and brought the coffin back to his old foundation in Shangyu.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother. His official service had been so scrupulously clean that his wife and children could not support themselves; he gave up his household goods and brought her coffin back to his old home in Shangyu.

sentences.zh: 畢，為子標之求安復令，隨子之官。

translations.literal: When finished, he sought for his son Biaozhi the post of magistrate of Anfu and followed the son to his post.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning was over, he secured the magistracy of Anfu for his son Biaozhi and went with him to his post.

sentences.zh: 服闋，為征西道規司馬、南平太守。

translations.literal: When mourning was completed, he was made Western Campaign Aide to Daogui and prefect of Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he became western campaign aide to Liu Daogui and prefect of Nanping.

sentences.zh: 徐道覆逼江陵，加鎮之建威將軍，統檀道濟、到彥之等討道覆，以不經將帥，固辭，不見聽。

translations.literal: When Xu Daofu pressed Jiangling, Zhenzhi was added as General Who Establishes Might, commanding Tan Daoji, Dao Yanzhi, and others to attack Daofu; because he had not passed through the ranks of generals and commanders, he firmly declined and was not heard.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Daofu threatened Jiangling, Zhenzhi was made General Who Establishes Might and placed over Tan Daoji, Dao Yanzhi, and others to suppress Daofu. He firmly declined on the ground that he had never served as a field commander, but his plea was rejected.

sentences.zh: 既而前軍失利，白衣領職，尋復本官。

translations.literal: Soon after the vanguard was defeated, he held office in plain dress; shortly he was restored to his original post.
translations.idiomatic: When the vanguard was defeated he was briefly reduced to commoner status, then soon restored to his former rank.

sentences.zh: 以討道覆功，封華容縣五等男，徵廷尉。

translations.literal: For merit in attacking Daofu, he was enfeoffed as fifth-rank Baron of Huarong County and summoned as Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: For his part in defeating Daofu he was enfeoffed as fifth-rank baron of Huarong and summoned to be minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 晉穆帝何皇后山陵，領將作大匠。

translations.literal: For Jin Emperor Mudi's Empress He's mountain tomb, he headed the Office of the Master of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw construction of the tomb mound for Empress He, consort of Emperor Mudi of Jin.

sentences.zh: 遷御史中丞，秉正不撓，百僚憚之。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Imperial Censor-in-Chief, upright and unbending; the hundred officials feared him.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to imperial censor-in-chief, upright and unyielding, and the whole bureaucracy stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 出為使持節、都督交、廣二州諸軍事、建威將軍、平越中郎將、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out as Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander of all military affairs of Jiao and Guang provinces, General Who Establishes Might, General of the Household Who Pacifies Yue, and Inspector of Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out bearing the staff of authority as commander of military affairs in Jiao and Guang, General Who Establishes Might, General of the Household Who Pacifies Yue, and inspector of Guang Province.

sentences.zh: 高祖謂人曰：「王鎮之少著清績，必將繼美吳隱之。

translations.literal: The Founder Emperor said to people: 'Wang Zhenzhi in youth has shown pure achievements; he will surely continue the excellence of Wu Yinshi.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu told others, "Wang Zhenzhi has shown a clean record from early on; he is sure to follow in the footsteps of Wu Yinshi.

sentences.zh: 嶺南之弊，非此不康也。

translations.literal: The abuses of Lingnan, without this one, will not be made secure.'
translations.idiomatic: The ills of the Lingnan region will not be cured without him."

sentences.zh: 」在鎮不受俸祿，蕭然無所營。

translations.literal: In his command he did not accept salary and emoluments; desolate, he had nothing he pursued.
translations.idiomatic: In his post he refused salary and stipends and lived sparely, with no private ventures.

sentences.zh: 去官之日，不異始至。

translations.literal: On the day he left office, he was no different from when he first arrived.
translations.idiomatic: When he left office he was no richer than when he had arrived.

sentences.zh: 高祖初建相國府，以為諮議參軍，領錄事。

translations.literal: When the Founder Emperor first established the Chancellor's Office, he was made Advisory Aide and headed the Records Office.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu first set up the chancellor's office, Zhenzhi was made advisory aide and head of records.

sentences.zh: 善於吏職，嚴而不殘。

translations.literal: He was skilled in the duties of officials, strict but not cruel.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at administrative duty—strict but not harsh.

sentences.zh: 遷宋臺祠部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Rites of the Song Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to minister of rites of the Song terrace.

sentences.zh: 高祖踐阼，鎮之以腳患自陳，出為輔國將軍、琅邪太守，遷宣訓衛尉，領本州大中正。

translations.literal: When the Founder Emperor ascended the throne, Zhenzhi on account of foot ailment stated himself and went out as General Who Assists the State and prefect of Langye; he was transferred to Commandant of the Garrison for Instruction and headed the Grand Rectifier of his native province.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu took the throne, Zhenzhi cited a foot ailment and left the capital as General Who Assists the State and prefect of Langye, then became commandant of the garrison for instruction and grand rectifier of his native province.

sentences.zh: 永初三年，卒官，時年六十六。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongchu he died in office, aged sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongchu he died in office at the age of sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 弟弘之，在《隱逸傳》。

translations.literal: His younger brother Hongzhi is in the 'Recluses' biography.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Hongzhi is treated in the chapter on recluses.

sentences.zh: 杜慧度，交趾朱鸘人也。

translations.literal: Du Huidu was a man of Zhu'er in Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Du Huidu was a native of Zhu'er in Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 本屬京兆。

translations.literal: His clan originally belonged to Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: His family originally came from Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 曾祖元，為寧浦太守，遂居交趾。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yuan was prefect of Ningpu and thereafter dwelt in Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Du Yuan served as prefect of Ningpu and then settled in Jiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 父瑗，字道言，仕州府為日南、九德、交趾太守。

translations.literal: His father Yuan, style name Daoyan, served the provincial administration as prefect of Rinan, Jiude, and Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Du Yuan, courtesy name Daoyan, served the regional government as prefect of Rinan, Jiude, and Jiaozhi in turn.

sentences.zh: 初，九真太守李遜父子勇壯有權力，威制交土，聞刺史騰遯之當至，分遣二子斷遏水陸津要。

translations.literal: At first, Rinan prefect Li Xun, father and sons, were brave and strong with power, awe-controlling the Jiao region; hearing that Inspector Teng Dunzhi was about to arrive, they separately sent two sons to cut off and block the water and land passes and key points.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Li Xun, prefect of Jiuzhen, and his sons were bold and powerful and dominated the Jiao region. Learning that Inspector Teng Dunzhi was on his way, they sent two sons to seize the key passes by land and water.

sentences.zh: 瑗收眾斬遜，州境獲寧。

translations.literal: Yuan gathered troops and beheaded Xun; the province's territory obtained peace.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan gathered forces, executed Xun, and restored peace in the province.

sentences.zh: 除龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of Soaring Dragon.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed General of Soaring Dragon.

sentences.zh: 遯之在州十餘年，與林邑累相攻伐。

translations.literal: Dunzhi was in the province more than ten years, with Linyi repeatedly attacking and campaigning against each other.
translations.idiomatic: Dunzhi spent more than ten years in the province, fighting repeatedly with Linyi.

sentences.zh: 遯之將北還，林邑王范胡達攻破日南、九德、九真三郡，遂圍州城。

translations.literal: When Dunzhi was about to return north, the king of Linyi Fan Huda attacked and broke Rinan, Jiude, and Jiuzhen commanderies, then besieged the provincial capital.
translations.idiomatic: As Dunzhi prepared to return north, the king of Linyi, Fan Huda, overran Rinan, Jiude, and Jiuzhen and then besieged the provincial capital.

sentences.zh: 時遯之去已遠，瑗與第三子玄之悉力固守，多設權策，累戰，大破之。

translations.literal: At that time Dunzhi had already gone far; Yuan with his third son Xuanzhi used all strength to defend firmly, set many stratagems, fought repeatedly, and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Dunzhi was already far away. Yuan and his third son Xuanzhi defended with all their strength, devised many stratagems, fought battle after battle, and routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 追討於九真、日南。

translations.literal: They pursued and attacked in Jiuzhen and Rinan.
translations.idiomatic: They pursued the foe through Jiuzhen and Rinan.

sentences.zh: 連捷，故胡達走還林邑。

translations.literal: Victories followed in succession, so Huda fled back to Linyi.
translations.idiomatic: Victory followed victory until Huda fled back to Linyi.

sentences.zh: 乃以瑗為龍驤將軍、交州刺史。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yuan was made General of Soaring Dragon and Inspector of Jiao Province.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan was then appointed General of Soaring Dragon and inspector of Jiao Province.

sentences.zh: 義旗進號冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: When the Banner of Righteousness advanced, his title was raised to General Who Champions the State.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous banner rose, his rank was raised to General Who Champions the State.

sentences.zh: 盧循竊據廣州，遣使通好，瑗斬之。

translations.literal: Lu Xun seized and held Guang Province, sent envoys to open friendly relations; Yuan beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Xun had seized Guangzhou and sent envoys seeking friendship; Yuan had them executed.

sentences.zh: 義熙六年，年八十四，卒，追贈右將軍，本官如故。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yixi, aged eighty-four, he died; posthumously enfeoffed as General of the Right, original office as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yixi he died at eighty-four and was posthumously made General of the Right with his former titles preserved.

sentences.zh: 慧度，瑗第五子也。

translations.literal: Huidu was Yuan's fifth son.
translations.idiomatic: Huidu was Yuan's fifth son.

sentences.zh: 初為州主簿，流民督護，遷九真太守。

translations.literal: At first he was provincial chief clerk, Protector of Displaced Populations, and was transferred to prefect of Jiuzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He began as provincial chief clerk and protector of displaced populations, then became prefect of Jiuzhen.

sentences.zh: 瑗卒，府州綱佐以交土接寇，不宜曠職，共推慧度行州府事，辭不就。

translations.literal: When Yuan died, the province and prefecture's leading aides, because the Jiao region bordered invaders, considered it unsuitable to leave the post vacant, jointly pushed Huidu to conduct provincial and prefectural affairs; he declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan died, the leading officials of the province argued that with enemies on the border the post could not stay empty and jointly urged Huidu to run provincial affairs; he refused.

sentences.zh: 七年，除使持節、督交州諸軍事、廣武將軍、交州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed Bearer of the Staff, Commander of all military affairs of Jiao Province, General of Expansive Might, and Inspector of Jiao Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was appointed bearer of the staff, commander of military affairs in Jiao, General of Expansive Might, and inspector of Jiao.

sentences.zh: 詔書未至，其年春，盧循襲破合浦，徑向交州。

translations.literal: Before the imperial edict arrived, that spring Lu Xun raided and broke Hepu, going straight toward Jiao Province.
translations.idiomatic: Before the edict arrived, that spring Lu Xun stormed Hepu and marched straight on Jiao.

sentences.zh: 慧度乃率文武六千人距循於石碕，交戰，禽循長史孫建之。

translations.literal: Huidu then led six thousand civil and military men to resist Xun at Shiji, joined battle, and captured Xun's chief clerk Sun Jianzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Huidu then led six thousand officials and troops to meet Xun at Shiji, fought him, and captured his chief clerk Sun Jianzhi.

sentences.zh: 循雖敗，餘黨猶有三千人，皆習練兵事。

translations.literal: Though Xun was defeated, his remaining partisans still had three thousand men, all practiced in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Though Xun was beaten, three thousand seasoned fighters remained in his ranks.

sentences.zh: 李子遜李弈、李脫等奔竄石碕，盤結俚、獠，各有部曲。

translations.literal: Li Zixun, Li Yi, Li Tuo, and others fled and scattered at Shiji, entrenched with Li and Liao peoples, each with their own followings.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zixun, Li Yi, Li Tuo, and others fled to Shiji, where they entrenched themselves among the Li and Liao peoples, each with his own band.

sentences.zh: 循知弈等與杜氏有怨，遣使招之，弈等引諸俚帥眾五六千人，受循節度。

translations.literal: Xun knew Yi and the others bore grudges against the Du clan, sent envoys to recruit them; Yi and the others led various Li chiefs with forces of five or six thousand, accepting Xun's command.
translations.idiomatic: Xun knew the Li brothers bore a grudge against the Du family and sent envoys to recruit them. They brought Li chieftains and five or six thousand men under Xun's command.

sentences.zh: 六月庚子，循晨造南津，命三軍入城乃食。

translations.literal: On the gengzi day of the sixth month, Xun at dawn reached Nanjin, ordering the three armies to enter the city before eating.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengzi day of the sixth month Xun reached Nanjin at dawn and ordered his three armies not to eat until they had entered the city.

sentences.zh: 慧度悉出宗族私財，以充勸賞。

translations.literal: Huidu brought out all the clan's private wealth to fill rewards for encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Huidu poured out his clan's private wealth to pay battle rewards.

sentences.zh: 弟交趾太守慧期、九真太守章民並督率水步軍，慧度自登高艦，合戰，放火箭雉尾炬，步軍夾兩岸射之。

translations.literal: His younger brother Jiaozhi prefect Huigi and Jiuzhen prefect Zhang Min both commanded water and land armies; Huidu himself boarded a tall warship, joined battle, loosed fire arrows and pheasant-tail torches, and infantry on both banks shot at them.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Huigi, prefect of Jiaozhi, and Zhang Min, prefect of Jiuzhen, led the land and river forces while Huidu boarded a tall warship. In the combined battle they loosed fire arrows and pheasant-tail torches while infantry on both banks rained shots on the enemy.

sentences.zh: 循眾艦俱然，一時散潰，循中箭赴水死。

translations.literal: All of Xun's ships caught fire together; in one moment they scattered and collapsed; Xun was struck by an arrow, went into the water, and died.
translations.idiomatic: All of Xun's ships burst into flame at once and his force broke apart. Xun took an arrow and died in the water.

sentences.zh: 斬循及父嘏，並循二子，親屬錄事參軍阮靜、中兵參軍羅農夫、李脫等，傳首京邑。

translations.literal: They beheaded Xun and his father Gu, together with Xun's two sons, kinsmen Recorder Aide Ruan Jing, Central Army Aide Luo Nongfu, Li Tuo, and others, and sent the heads to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: They beheaded Xun, his father Gu, his two sons, and such associates as recorder aide Ruan Jing, central army aide Luo Nongfu, and Li Tuo, and sent the heads to the capital.

sentences.zh: 封慧度龍編縣侯，食邑千戶。

translations.literal: Huidu was enfeoffed as Marquis of Longbian County with a fief of a thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Huidu was enfeoffed as marquis of Longbian with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 高祖踐阼，進號輔國將軍。

translations.literal: When the Founder Emperor ascended the throne, Huidu's title was advanced to General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne, Huidu was promoted to General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 其年，率文武萬人南討林邑，所殺過半，前後被抄略，悉得還本。

translations.literal: That year he led ten thousand civil and military men south to attack Linyi; those killed were more than half; persons previously carried off in raids all obtained return to their origins.
translations.idiomatic: That year he led ten thousand officials and troops south against Linyi, killing more than half the enemy and recovering all who had been carried off in earlier raids.

sentences.zh: 林邑乞降，輸生口、大象、金銀、古貝等，乃釋之。

translations.literal: Linyi begged to surrender, presenting living captives, elephants, gold and silver, ancient shell currency, and the like; he then released them.
translations.idiomatic: Linyi sued for peace, offering captives, elephants, gold, silver, cowrie shells, and other goods, and he let them go.

sentences.zh: 遣長史江悠奉表獻捷。

translations.literal: He sent Chief Clerk Jiang You to present a memorial reporting victory.
translations.idiomatic: He sent chief clerk Jiang You to the court with a memorial reporting victory.

sentences.zh: 慧度布衣蔬食，儉約質素，能彈琴，頗好《莊》、《老》。

translations.literal: Huidu wore plain cloth and ate vegetables, was frugal, simple, and unadorned, could play the zither, and rather favored the Zhuangzi and Laozi.
translations.idiomatic: Huidu dressed in plain cloth and ate simple food, living frugally and without ornament. He played the zither and was fond of Zhuangzi and Laozi.

sentences.zh: 禁斷淫祀，崇脩學校。

translations.literal: He forbade and cut off licentious sacrifices and honored and repaired schools.
translations.idiomatic: He banned improper cults and promoted the schools.

sentences.zh: 歲荒民饑，則以私祿賑給。

translations.literal: In years of famine when the people hungered, he used private salary to relieve and supply them.
translations.idiomatic: In years of famine he used his private salary to feed the people.

sentences.zh: 為政纖密，有如治家，由是威惠沾洽，姦盜不起，乃至城門不夜閉，道不拾遺。

translations.literal: In governing he was fine and close, as if managing a household; from this authority and grace soaked through in harmony, treachery and theft did not arise, reaching even to city gates not closed at night and roads where none picked up lost things.
translations.idiomatic: He governed with the meticulous care of a household head, so that his authority and kindness spread together, crime vanished, city gates stood unbarred at night, and no one picked up lost goods in the streets.

sentences.zh: 少帝景平元年，卒，時年五十，追贈左將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Emperor Shaodi's Jingping era he died, aged fifty; posthumously enfeoffed as General of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingping under Emperor Shaodi he died at fifty and was posthumously made General of the Left.

sentences.zh: 以慧度長子員外散騎侍郎弘文為振威將軍、刺史。

translations.literal: Huidu's eldest son, Outside-the-Court Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary Hongwen, was made General Who Quells Might and Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Huidu's eldest son Hongwen, an outside attendant cavalier, was made General Who Quells Might and inspector.

sentences.zh: 初，高祖北征關、洛，慧度板弘文為鷹揚將軍，流民督護，配兵三千，北係大軍。

translations.literal: At first, when the Founder Emperor campaigned north against Guan and Luo, Huidu appointed Hongwen on commission as General of the Soaring Hawk, Protector of Displaced Populations, with an allotment of three thousand troops to tie north to the great army.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Gaozu marched north against Guan and Luoyang, Huidu commissioned Hongwen as General of the Soaring Hawk and protector of displaced populations with three thousand men to join the main army in the north.

sentences.zh: 行至廣州，關、洛已平，乃歸。

translations.literal: When he reached Guang Province, Guan and Luo were already pacified, so he returned.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Guangzhou only to learn that Guan and Luoyang were already pacified, and turned back.

sentences.zh: 統府板弘文行九真太守。

translations.literal: The governing office commissioned Hongwen to act as prefect of Jiuzhen.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial headquarters commissioned him acting prefect of Jiuzhen.

sentences.zh: 及繼父為刺史，亦以寬和得眾，襲爵龍編侯。

translations.literal: When he succeeded his father as inspector, he also by lenience and harmony won the masses, and inherited the title Marquis of Longbian.
translations.idiomatic: When he succeeded his father as inspector he likewise won the people through lenience and harmony and inherited the marquisate of Longbian.

sentences.zh: 太祖元嘉四年，以廷尉王徽為交州刺史，弘文就徴。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanjia under the Founding Emperor, Minister of Justice Wang Hui was made Inspector of Jiao Province; Hongwen went to answer the summons.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yuanjia, Emperor Taizu appointed Minister of Justice Wang Hui inspector of Jiao, and Hongwen was summoned to yield the post.

sentences.zh: 會得重疾，牽以就路，親舊見其患篤，勸表待病癒。

translations.literal: He happened to contract a severe illness; pulled along he took the road; relatives and friends seeing his ailment grave urged him to memorialize and wait until the illness healed.
translations.idiomatic: He fell gravely ill but was dragged onto the road anyway. Kin and friends, seeing how serious his illness was, urged him to petition and wait until he recovered.

sentences.zh: 弘文曰：「吾世荷皇恩，杖節三世，常欲投軀帝庭，以報所荷。

translations.literal: Hongwen said: 'Our house for generations has borne the imperial grace; bearing the staff for three generations, I have constantly wished to cast my body before the imperial court to repay what I have borne.'
translations.idiomatic: Hongwen said, "Our family has borne the emperor's grace for generations. For three generations we have held the staff of office, and I have long wished to offer my life at court in repayment."

sentences.zh: 況親被徵命，而可宴然者乎！

translations.literal: How much more when I personally receive the summons—how could I be at ease!'
translations.idiomatic: How much more now that I have been summoned in person—how could I rest at ease!"

sentences.zh: 如其顛沛，此乃命也。

translations.literal: If I suffer hardship and distress, this is fate.'
translations.idiomatic: If I come to ruin on the way, that will be fate."

sentences.zh: 」弘文母既年老，見弘文輿疾就路，不忍分別，相與俱行。

translations.literal: Hongwen's mother was already old; seeing Hongwen in a litter taking the road, she could not bear to part and traveled together with him.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwen's mother was already old. Seeing her son carried off ill on the road, she could not bear to part from him and went along with him.

sentences.zh: 到廣州，遂卒。

translations.literal: Upon reaching Guang Province, he thereupon died.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Guangzhou, he died there.

sentences.zh: 臨死，遣弟弘猷詣京，朝廷甚哀之。

translations.literal: Facing death, he sent his younger brother Hongyou to proceed to the capital; the court greatly mourned him.
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed he sent his younger brother Hongyou to the capital, and the court deeply grieved for him.

sentences.zh: 徐豁，字萬同，東莞姑幕人也，中散大夫廣兄子。

translations.literal: Xu Huo, styled Wantong, was a man of Gumu in Dongguan, nephew of Palace Attendant-in-Ordinary Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Huo, courtesy name Wantong, came from Gumu in Dongguan commandery and was a nephew of Xu Guang, palace attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 父邈，晉太子左衛率。

translations.literal: His father Miao was Left Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard in Jin.
translations.idiomatic: His father Miao had been left commandant of the crown prince's guard under Jin.

sentences.zh: 豁晉安帝隆安末為太學博士。

translations.literal: At the end of the Long'an era of Jin Emperor An, Huo was an Erudite of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Long'an reign of Emperor An of Jin, Huo served as an erudite of the imperial academy.

sentences.zh: 桓玄輔政，為中外都督，豁議：「致敬唯內外武官，太宰、司徒，並非軍職，則琅邪王不應加敬。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan held regency as Grand Commander of Inner and Outer Forces, Huo argued: 'Salutations should be rendered only by inner and outer military officials. The Grand Tutor and Grand Marshal are not military posts, so the Prince of Langye should not be required to render additional salutations.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan held the regency as grand commander of inner and outer forces, Huo argued: "Salutations should be required only of inner and outer military officials. The grand tutor and grand marshal are not military posts, so the Prince of Langye ought not be made to render such salutes.

sentences.zh: 」玄諷中丞免豁官。

translations.literal: ' Xuan prompted the censor-in-chief to dismiss Huo from office.
translations.idiomatic: " Huan Xuan induced the censor-in-chief to dismiss Huo from office.

sentences.zh: 玄敗，以為秘書郎，尚書倉部郎，右軍何無忌功曹，仍為鎮南參軍；

translations.literal: When Xuan was defeated, Huo was made Secretary Gentleman, Director of the Storage Bureau in the Ministry of Works, Administrative Aide under He Wuji of the Right Army, and thereafter Military Aide to the Army Who Guards the South;
translations.idiomatic: After Huan Xuan's defeat, Huo was appointed secretary gentleman, director of the storage bureau in the ministry of works, administrative aide to He Wuji of the right army, and then military aide to the army who guards the south;

sentences.zh: 又祠部，永世令，建武司馬，中軍參軍，尚書左丞。

translations.literal: also [served in] Sacrificial Affairs, as Magistrate of Yongshi, Army Aide to the Army Who Establishes Might, Military Aide to the Central Army, and Left Assistant Director in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: he also served in sacrificial affairs, as magistrate of Yongshi, army aide to the army who establishes might, military aide to the central army, and left assistant director in the ministry of works.

sentences.zh: 永初初，為徐羨之鎮軍司馬，尚書左丞，山陰令。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongchu, he was Army Aide to the Army-in-Chief under Xu Xianzhi, Left Assistant Director in the Ministry of Works, and Magistrate of Shanyin.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yongchu era he became army aide to the army-in-chief under Xu Xianzhi, left assistant director in the ministry of works, and magistrate of Shanyin.

sentences.zh: 歷二丞三邑，精練明理，為一世所推。

translations.literal: Having served twice as assistant director and thrice as magistrate, he was expert, practiced, and clear in principle, and was esteemed by his generation.
translations.idiomatic: Having served twice as assistant director and three times as magistrate, he was skilled, experienced, and clear in judgment, and his generation held him in high regard.

sentences.zh: 元嘉初，為始興太守。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanjia, he was Prefect of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yuanjia era he was made prefect of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 三年，遣大使巡行四方，並使郡縣各言損益。

translations.literal: In the third year, grand commissioners were sent to tour the four quarters, and each commandery and county was also ordered to report what should be reduced or increased.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year the court sent grand commissioners to tour the realm and ordered every commandery and county to report what policies should be cut back or expanded.

sentences.zh: 豁因此表陳三事，其一曰：「郡大田，武吏年滿十六，便課米六十斛，十五以下至十三，皆課米三十斛，一戶內隨丁多少，悉皆輸米。

translations.literal: Huo therefore submitted a memorial setting forth three matters. The first stated: 'In the commandery's chief fields, when military conscript males reach sixteen years of age, they are assessed sixty hu of grain; from fifteen down to thirteen, all are assessed thirty hu of grain. Within each household, according to however many males there are, all must deliver grain.
translations.idiomatic: Huo therefore submitted a memorial on three matters. The first read: "In this commandery's chief fields, military conscripts who reach sixteen are assessed sixty hu of grain; from fifteen down to thirteen, each is assessed thirty hu. Every household must deliver grain according to however many males it contains.

sentences.zh: 且十三歲兒，未堪田作，或是單迥，無相兼通，年及應輸，便自逃逸，既遏接蠻、俚，去就益易。

translations.literal: Moreover, thirteen-year-old children cannot yet bear field work; some are solitary and isolated, with no mutual support; when the year arrives and they should pay tribute, they flee on their own. Since [this region] borders the Man and Li peoples, coming and going becomes all the easier.
translations.idiomatic: Thirteen-year-olds cannot yet work the fields. Some households stand alone with no one to share the burden; when the year of assessment arrives they simply flee. Because this region borders Man and Li territory, leaving and returning is all too easy.

sentences.zh: 或乃斷截支體，產子不養，戶口歲減，實此之由。

translations.literal: Some even mutilate limbs or abandon newborn children; household population declines year by year — this is truly the cause.
translations.idiomatic: Some even mutilate their limbs or abandon newborn children. The population shrinks year by year, and this is the real reason.

sentences.zh: 謂宜更量課限，使得存立。

translations.literal: I submit that the assessment limits should be recalibrated so that [people] can survive and stand.
translations.idiomatic: The assessment limits should be recalibrated so that people can survive.

sentences.zh: 今若減其米課，雖有交損，考之將來，理有深益。

translations.literal: If the grain levy were now reduced, although there would be immediate mutual loss, considered for the future, there would be profound benefit in principle.
translations.idiomatic: If the grain levy were reduced now, there would be an immediate shortfall, but judged by the future, the long-term gain would be great.

sentences.zh: 」其二曰：「郡領銀民三百餘戶，鑿坑采砂，皆二三丈。

translations.literal: ' The second stated: 'The commandery oversees more than three hundred households of silver workers who dig pits and mine ore, all two or three zhang deep.
translations.idiomatic: " The second read: "More than three hundred households of silver miners in this commandery dig pits two or three zhang deep to extract ore.

sentences.zh: 功役既苦，不顧崩壓，一歲之中，每有死者。

translations.literal: The labor is so bitter that they heed not cave-ins; within a single year, there are deaths every so often.
translations.idiomatic: The work is so grueling that they ignore the risk of collapse, and every year people die in the pits.

sentences.zh: 官司檢切，猶致逋違，老少相隨，永絕農業；

translations.literal: Though official pressure is strict and pressing, they still fail to meet quotas; old and young follow one another, forever abandoning agriculture;
translations.idiomatic: Even under strict official pressure they still fail to meet quotas. Old and young alike are drawn into the mines and abandon farming forever;

sentences.zh: 千有餘口，皆資他食，豈唯一夫不耕，或受其饑而已。

translations.literal: more than a thousand mouths all depend on others for food — it is not merely that one man fails to plow and others go hungry.
translations.idiomatic: more than a thousand mouths depend on others for food. The harm is not simply that one man fails to plow while others go hungry.

sentences.zh: 所以歲有不稔，便致甚困。

translations.literal: Therefore when the year is not bountiful, severe hardship follows.
translations.idiomatic: That is why any lean year brings severe distress.

sentences.zh: 尋臺邸用米，不異於銀，謂宜准銀課米，即事為便。

translations.literal: Considering that the capital offices use grain no differently from silver, I submit that the silver levy should be converted to a grain levy on the same standard — this would be convenient in practice.
translations.idiomatic: Since the capital offices use grain no less than silver, the silver levy should be converted to a grain levy on the same standard. That would be the practical course.

sentences.zh: 」其三曰：「中宿縣俚民課銀，一子丁輸南稱半兩。

translations.literal: ' The third stated: 'In Zhongsu County, Li people are assessed silver: each adult male pays half a liang by the southern scale.
translations.idiomatic: " The third read: "In Zhongsu County the Li people are assessed silver: each adult male pays half a liang by the southern weight standard.

sentences.zh: 尋此縣自不出銀，又俚民皆巢居鳥語，不閑貨易之宜，每至買銀，為損已甚。

translations.literal: This county itself produces no silver; moreover the Li people all live in tree nests and speak their own tongues, unskilled in the ways of trade; whenever they must buy silver, the loss to them is very severe.
translations.idiomatic: That county produces no silver of its own, and the Li live in tree nests and speak their own languages, knowing nothing of trade. Whenever they must buy silver to pay the tax, the cost to them is crushing.

sentences.zh: 又稱兩受入，易生姦巧，山俚愚怯，不辨自申，官所課甚輕，民以所輸為劇。

translations.literal: Also, weighing by the liang for intake easily gives rise to fraud; the mountain Li are simple and timid, unable to plead for themselves; what the government assesses is very light, yet what the people must deliver they find oppressive.
translations.idiomatic: Weighing silver by the liang at collection also invites fraud. The mountain Li are simple and timid and cannot plead their own case. The official assessment seems light, yet what the people must actually deliver feels unbearably heavy.

sentences.zh: 今若聽計丁課米，公私兼利。」

translations.literal: If they were now permitted to pay grain assessed by head count, both public and private interests would benefit.'
translations.idiomatic: If they were allowed to pay grain assessed by head count instead, both the state and the people would benefit."

sentences.zh: 在郡著績，太祖嘉之。

translations.literal: His achievements in the commandery were outstanding; the Founder Emperor praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He distinguished himself in the commandery, and Emperor Wu praised him.

sentences.zh: 下詔曰：「始興太守豁，潔己退食，恪居在官，政事脩理，惠澤沾被。

translations.literal: An edict was issued: 'Shixing Prefect Huo keeps himself pure, eats frugally, maintains reverent conduct in office, puts government in good order, and spreads his grace far and wide.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued: "Shixing Prefect Huo keeps himself pure, eats frugally, maintains reverent conduct in office, governs well, and spreads his kindness far and wide.

sentences.zh: 近嶺南荒弊，郡境尤甚，拯恤有方，濟厥饑饉，雖古之良守，蔑以尚焉。

translations.literal: Recently Lingnan has been desolate and impoverished, and this commandery's territory is especially so; yet he has had effective methods of relief and succor, delivering [the people] from famine — even the good prefects of antiquity could scarcely surpass this.
translations.idiomatic: Lingnan has lately been desolate and impoverished, and his commandery especially so, yet he found effective ways to relieve and succor the people through famine. Even the finest prefects of antiquity could scarcely match him.

sentences.zh: 宜蒙褒賁，以旌清績，可賜絹二百匹，穀千斛。

translations.literal: He should receive commendation and reward to mark his pure achievements; he may be granted two hundred bolts of silk and one thousand hu of grain.'
translations.idiomatic: He should receive commendation and reward to mark his clean record. Let him be granted two hundred bolts of silk and one thousand hu of grain."

sentences.zh: 」五年，以為持節、督廣、交二州諸軍事、寧遠將軍、平越中郎將、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he was made Bearer of the Staff, Commander of all military affairs in Guang and Jiao provinces, General of Distant Peace, General of the Household Who Pacifies Yue, and Inspector of Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was appointed bearer of the staff, commander of military affairs in Guang and Jiao provinces, General of Distant Peace, General of the Household Who Pacifies Yue, and inspector of Guang Province.

sentences.zh: 未拜，卒，時年五十一。

translations.literal: Before he could assume the post he died, aged fifty-one.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could take up the appointment he died, at the age of fifty-one.

sentences.zh: 太祖又下詔曰：「豁廉清勤恪，著稱所司，故擢授南服，申其才志。

translations.literal: The Founder Emperor again issued an edict: 'Huo was known throughout his offices for integrity, purity, diligence, and reverence; therefore he was promoted to the southern territories to give full scope to his talents and intent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again issued an edict: "Huo was renowned in every office for integrity, purity, diligence, and devotion. That is why he was promoted to the south, to give full scope to his talent and ambition.

sentences.zh: 不幸喪殞，朕甚悼之。

translations.literal: Unfortunately he died untimely; I deeply mourn him.
translations.idiomatic: He has died untimely, and I deeply mourn him.

sentences.zh: 可賜錢十萬，布百匹，以營葬事。」

translations.literal: He may be granted one hundred thousand cash, one hundred bolts of cloth, to cover funeral arrangements.'
translations.idiomatic: Let him be granted one hundred thousand cash and one hundred bolts of cloth for his funeral arrangements."

sentences.zh: 陸徽，字休猷，吳郡吳人也。

translations.literal: Lu Hui, styled Xiuyou, was a man of Wu in Wu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Hui, courtesy name Xiuyou, came from Wu in Wu commandery.

sentences.zh: 郡辟命主簿，仍除衛軍、車騎二府參軍，揚州主簿，王弘衛將軍主簿，除尚書都官郎，出補建康令。

translations.literal: The commandery summoned him as chief clerk; he was then appointed military aide in the Guard Army and Cavalry General's offices, chief clerk of Yang Province, chief clerk to Wang Hong as General of the Guard, promoted to Director of Punishments in the Ministry of Works, and sent out to fill the post of Magistrate of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery recruited him as chief clerk. He was then made military aide in the guard army and cavalry general's offices, chief clerk of Yang Province, and chief clerk to Wang Hong as general of the guard. He was promoted to director of punishments in the ministry of works and sent out to serve as magistrate of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 清平無私，為太祖所善，遷司徒左西掾。

translations.literal: Pure, fair, and without partiality, he was favored by the Founder Emperor and was transferred to Left Western Aide on the Grand Marshal's staff.
translations.idiomatic: Pure, fair, and impartial, he won the emperor's favor and was transferred to left western aide on the grand marshal's staff.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十四年，為始興太守。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Yuanjia, he was Prefect of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year of Yuanjia he was made prefect of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 明年，仍除使持節、交、廣二州諸軍事、綏遠將軍、平越中郎將、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: The following year he was again appointed Bearer of the Staff, Commander of military affairs in Jiao and Guang, General Who Pacifies the Distance, General of the Household Who Pacifies Yue, and Inspector of Guang Province.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was again appointed bearer of the staff, commander of military affairs in Jiao and Guang, General Who Pacifies the Distance, General of the Household Who Pacifies Yue, and inspector of Guang Province.

sentences.zh: 清名亞王鎮之，為士民所愛詠。

translations.literal: His reputation for purity ranked just below Wang Zhenzhi's, and gentry and common people loved to praise and sing of him.
translations.idiomatic: His reputation for integrity ranked just below Wang Zhenzhi's, and gentry and common people alike loved to praise him.

sentences.zh: 上表薦士曰：「臣聞陵雪褒潁，貞柯必振；

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial recommending a scholar, saying: 'I have heard that when snow buries the peaks, Song and Ying are praised — the upright trunk will surely stand firm;
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial recommending a scholar, saying: "I have heard that when snow buries the peaks, the fir and cypress of Song and Ying are praised, and the upright trunk will surely stand firm;

sentences.zh: 尊風賞流，清原斯挹。

translations.literal: when lofty winds honor the current, the clear spring is thereby drawn from.
translations.idiomatic: when lofty winds honor the stream, the clear spring is drawn from in turn.

sentences.zh: 是以衣囊揮譽於西京，折轅延高於東帝。

translations.literal: Thus one earned fame through robe and purse in the Western Capital, and a broken axle drew in the lofty man under the Eastern Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Zhu Maichen won renown with nothing but robe and purse in the Western Capital, and a broken carriage axle drew in a lofty man for the Eastern Emperor.

sentences.zh: 伏見廣州別駕從事史朱萬嗣，年五十三，字少豫，理業沖夷，秉操純白，行稱私庭，能著官政。

translations.literal: I humbly observe Assistant Administrator and Attendant Clerk Zhu Wansyi of Guangzhou, aged fifty-three, styled Shaoyu, whose learning and occupation are serene and modest, whose conduct is pure white, whose behavior is praised within the family, and whose ability shows in official governance.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly observe Zhu Wansyi, assistant administrator and attendant clerk of Guangzhou, aged fifty-three, courtesy name Shaoyu. His learning is serene and modest, his conduct pure, his private life exemplary, and his ability evident in public office.

sentences.zh: 雖氏非世祿，宦無通資，而隨牒南服，位極僚首，九綜州綱，三端府職，頻掌蕃機，屢績符守。

translations.literal: Although his clan has no hereditary stipend and his official career no ready resources, he followed his appointment to the southern regions, reaching the head of the staff; nine times he has mastered the commandery framework, thrice he has held key posts in the prefecture, repeatedly handling frontier affairs, and repeatedly achieving merit as inspector and prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Although his family holds no hereditary stipend and his career had no ready patronage, he followed his appointments to the south and rose to the head of the staff. Nine times he has mastered a commandery's affairs, thrice he has held key posts in a prefecture, repeatedly handled frontier business, and repeatedly distinguished himself as inspector and prefect.

sentences.zh: 年暨知命，廉尚愈高，冰心與貪流爭激，霜情與晚節彌茂。

translations.literal: His years have reached fifty; his integrity and elevation grow ever higher; his heart of ice contends fiercely with the stream of greed; his frosty disposition and late-season integrity flourish all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Now past fifty, his integrity grows ever higher. His heart of ice contends fiercely with the stream of greed, and his frosty resolve and late-season virtue flourish all the more.

sentences.zh: 歷宰金山，家無寶鏤之飾；

translations.literal: Having governed Jinshan, his home has no jewel-inlaid ornament;
translations.idiomatic: Though he governed Jinshan, his home had no jewel-inlaid ornament;

sentences.zh: 連組珠海，室靡璫珥之珍。

translations.literal: though linked in office chains to the Pearl River, his rooms lack jeweled ear pendants.
translations.idiomatic: though he served in office after office along the Pearl River, his rooms held no jeweled ear pendants.

sentences.zh: 確然守志，不求聞達，實足以澄革汙吏，洗鏡貪氓。

translations.literal: Firmly he keeps his intent, seeking no fame or advancement — truly enough to clarify and reform filthy officials and wash clean the mirror of greedy commoners.
translations.idiomatic: He steadfastly keeps to his principles and seeks no fame or advancement. Truly he is fit to clarify and reform corrupt officials and hold up a mirror to greedy commoners.

sentences.zh: 臣謬忝司牧，任專萬里，雖情祗慎擢，才闕豪露，敢罄愚陋，舉其所知。

translations.literal: Your servant unworthily holds the post of regional governor, charged with ten thousand li; though my feeling is reverently cautious in promotion and my talent lacks bold revelation, I dare exhaust my feeble ignorance and recommend one I know.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant unworthily holds the post of regional governor, charged with ten thousand li. Though I am reverently cautious in recommending men and lack the talent to display them boldly, I dare offer all my poor knowledge and recommend one I know.

sentences.zh: 如得提名禮闈，抗跡朝省，摶嶺表之清風，負冰宇之潔望，則恩融一臣，而施光萬物。

translations.literal: If he could be nominated at the ritual gate and take his place in the court ministries, spreading the pure breeze of the Lingnan region and bearing the clean renown of icy purity, then grace would penetrate one minister while its light would shine upon all things.
translations.idiomatic: If he could be nominated at the ritual gate and take his place in the court ministries, spreading the pure breeze of the Lingnan region and bearing a reputation for icy integrity, then grace would reach one minister while its light would shine on all things.

sentences.zh: 敢緣天澤云行，時德雨施，每甄外州，榮加遠國。

translations.literal: I venture to rely on heaven's grace moving like clouds and the season's virtue falling like rain, which each time selects from outer commanderies and adds honor to distant lands.
translations.idiomatic: I venture to rely on Your Majesty's grace moving like clouds and virtue falling like rain, which each time selects men from outer commanderies and adds honor to distant lands.

sentences.zh: 是以獻其瞽言，希垂聽覽。」

translations.literal: Therefore I offer this blind man's words, hoping they may receive your hearing.'
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I offer these blind words of mine, hoping they may receive your attention."

sentences.zh: 二十一年，徵以為南平王鑠冠軍司馬、長沙內史，行湘州府事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was summoned as Champion Army Aide to the Prince of Nanping, Shuo, Interior Minister of Changsha, and provisional head of the Xiangzhou prefecture office.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was summoned to serve as champion army aide to the Prince of Nanping, Shuo, interior minister of Changsha, and provisional head of the Xiangzhou prefecture office.

sentences.zh: 母憂去職。

translations.literal: On his mother's mourning he left office.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 張尋、趙廣為亂於益州，兵寇之餘，政荒民擾。

translations.literal: Zhang Xun and Zhao Guang raised rebellion in Yizhou; after military depredations, government was neglected and the people were harassed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xun and Zhao Guang raised rebellion in Yizhou. After the ravages of war, government collapsed and the people were in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，乃追徽為持節、督益、寧二州諸軍事、寧朔將軍、益州刺史。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was urgently recalled as Bearer of the Staff, Commander of military affairs in Yi and Ning provinces, General Who Pacifies the North, and Inspector of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he was urgently recalled as bearer of the staff, commander of military affairs in Yi and Ning provinces, General Who Pacifies the North, and inspector of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 隱恤有方，威惠兼著，寇盜靜息，民物殷阜，蜀土安說，至今稱之。

translations.literal: He had effective methods of discreet relief; both authority and kindness were manifest; bandits and robbers quieted; people and goods grew abundant; Shu lands were peaceful and content — to this day he is praised.
translations.idiomatic: He had effective methods of discreet relief. Both authority and kindness were manifest, bandits and robbers subsided, people and goods prospered, and Shu was peaceful and content. To this day he is still praised.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，卒，時年六十二。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he died, aged sixty-two.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he died, at the age of sixty-two.

sentences.zh: 身亡之日，家無餘財。

translations.literal: On the day he died, his household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he died his household had no surplus wealth.

sentences.zh: 太祖甚痛惜之，詔曰：「徽厲志廉潔，歷任恪勤，奉公盡誠，克己無倦。

translations.literal: The Founder Emperor deeply grieved and regretted this, and issued an edict: 'Hui set his will on integrity and purity, in every post was reverent and diligent, served the public with full sincerity, and restrained himself without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply grieved for him and issued an edict: "Hui set his heart on integrity and purity. In every post he was diligent and devoted, served the public with full sincerity, and restrained himself without weariness.

sentences.zh: 褒榮未申，不幸夙殞，言念在懷，以為傷恨。

translations.literal: Commendation and honor had not yet been extended; unfortunately he died untimely; thinking of this fills the heart with grief and regret.
translations.idiomatic: Commendation and honors had not yet been granted when he died untimely. The thought fills me with grief and regret.

sentences.zh: 可贈輔國將軍，本官如故。

translations.literal: He may be posthumously granted General Who Assists the State, his original office remaining as before.'
translations.idiomatic: Let him be posthumously made General Who Assists the State, with his former rank retained."

sentences.zh: 」賜錢十萬，米二百斛。

translations.literal: He was granted one hundred thousand cash and two hundred hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted one hundred thousand cash and two hundred hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 諡曰簡子。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Jianzi.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Jianzi, "The Simple."

sentences.zh: 子睿，正員外郎。

translations.literal: His son Rui was a Regular Outside Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rui served as a regular outside attendant.

sentences.zh: 弟展，臧質車騎長史、尋陽太守，質敗，從誅。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zhan was Chief Clerk to Zang Zhi as Cavalry General and Prefect of Xunyang; when Zhi was defeated, he was executed along with him.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zhan was chief clerk to Zang Zhi as cavalry general and prefect of Xunyang. When Zang Zhi was defeated, Zhan was executed with him.

sentences.zh: 阮長之，字茂景，陳留尉氏人也。

translations.literal: Ruan Changzhi, styled Maojing, was a man of Weishi in Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Changzhi, courtesy name Maojing, came from Weishi in Chenliu commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖思曠，金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His grandfather Sikuan was Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sikuan had been grand master of splendid happiness with the golden seal and purple ribbon.

sentences.zh: 父普，驃騎諮議參軍。

translations.literal: His father Pu was Advisory Aide to the Fast Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: His father Pu had been advisory aide to the fast cavalry general.

sentences.zh: 長之年十五喪父，有孝性，哀感傍人。

translations.literal: Changzhi at fifteen lost his father; he had a filial nature, and his grief moved those around him.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhi lost his father at fifteen. Deeply filial by nature, his grief moved all who saw him.

sentences.zh: 服除，蔬食者猶積載。

translations.literal: When mourning was completed, he still ate vegetables for accumulated years.
translations.idiomatic: Even after mourning ended he continued to eat plain food for years.

sentences.zh: 閒居篤學，未嘗有惰容。

translations.literal: Living in retirement he devoted himself to study and never showed a lazy countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Living quietly at home he devoted himself to study and never showed a lazy face.

sentences.zh: 初為諸府參軍，除員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: At first he was military aide in various offices and was appointed Outside-the-Court Cavalier Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as military aide in various offices and was appointed outside attendant cavalier.

sentences.zh: 母老，求補襄垣令，督郵無禮，鞭之，去職。

translations.literal: His mother was old; he sought appointment as Magistrate of Xiangyuan. A postal inspector was disrespectful, and he flogged him, then left office.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother grew old he sought appointment as magistrate of Xiangyuan. A postal inspector treated him disrespectfully, so he flogged the man and resigned.

sentences.zh: 尋補廬陵王義真車騎行正參軍，平越長史，東莞太守。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Acting Regular Military Aide to the Cavalry General under the Prince of Luling, Yizhen, Chief Clerk Who Pacifies Yue, and Prefect of Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed acting regular military aide to the cavalry general under the Prince of Luling, Yizhen, chief clerk who pacifies Yue, and prefect of Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 入為尚書殿中郎，出為武昌太守。

translations.literal: He entered [the capital] as Director in the Palace Secretariat and went out as Prefect of Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as director in the palace secretariat and went out again as prefect of Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 時王弘為江州，雅相知重，引為車騎從事中郎。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Hong was in charge of Jiang Province and greatly knew and valued him, bringing him in as Attendant Gentleman on the Cavalry General's staff.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wang Hong was in charge of Jiang Province and held him in high esteem, bringing him in as attendant gentleman on the cavalry general's staff.

sentences.zh: 入為太子中舍人，中書侍郎，以母老，固辭朝直，補彭城王義康平北諮議參軍。

translations.literal: He entered [the capital] as Palace Attendant to the Heir Apparent and Gentleman of the Secretariat, but because his mother was old he firmly declined palace duty and was appointed Advisory Aide Who Pacifies the North under the Prince of Pengcheng, Yikang.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as palace attendant to the heir apparent and gentleman of the secretariat, but because his mother was old he firmly declined palace duty and was appointed advisory aide who pacifies the north under the Prince of Pengcheng, Yikang.

sentences.zh: 元嘉九年，遷臨川內史，以南土卑濕，母年老，非所宜，辭不就。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yuanjia he was transferred to Interior Minister of Linchuan, but because the southern lands are low and damp and his mother was old — unsuitable for her — he declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Yuanjia he was transferred to interior minister of Linchuan, but because the south is low and damp and his mother was old, he declined the post as unsuitable.

sentences.zh: 十一年，復除臨海太守。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was again appointed Prefect of Linhai.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was again appointed prefect of Linhai.

sentences.zh: 至郡少時而母亡，葬畢，不勝憂，十四年，卒，時年五十九。

translations.literal: Not long after reaching the commandery his mother died; when the burial was completed, unable to bear grief, in the fourteenth year he died, aged fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Not long after he reached the commandery his mother died. When the burial was over he could not bear his grief, and in the fourteenth year he died, at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 時郡縣田祿，芒種為斷，此前去官者，則一年秩祿皆入前人；

translations.literal: At the time, salary from field revenues in commanderies and counties was reckoned at Grain-in-Ear; for those leaving office before this date, the full year's salary went to the predecessor;
translations.idiomatic: At the time, field-revenue salaries in commanderies and counties were reckoned at Grain-in-Ear. For an official who left before that date, the full year's salary went to his predecessor;

sentences.zh: 此後去官者，則一年秩祿皆入後人。

translations.literal: for those leaving after, the full year's salary went to the successor.
translations.idiomatic: for one who left after it, the full year's salary went to his successor.

sentences.zh: 始以元嘉末改此科，計月分祿。

translations.literal: It was only at the end of Yuanjia that this rule was changed, and salary was apportioned by month.
translations.idiomatic: Only at the end of the Yuanjia era was this rule changed, and salaries were apportioned by month.

sentences.zh: 長之去武昌郡，代人未至，以芒種前一日解印綬。

translations.literal: When Changzhi left Wuchang commandery, his replacement had not yet arrived; on the day before Grain-in-Ear he surrendered seal and cord.
translations.idiomatic: When Changzhi left Wuchang, his replacement had not yet arrived. He surrendered his seal and cord on the day before Grain-in-Ear.

sentences.zh: 初發京師，親故或以器物贈別，得便緘錄，後歸，悉以還之。

translations.literal: When he first set out from the capital, relatives and friends sometimes gave him objects as parting gifts; when convenient he sealed and recorded them, and on returning later he returned them all.
translations.idiomatic: When he first set out from the capital, relatives and friends sometimes gave him parting gifts. He sealed and recorded each item when he could, and on his return he restored them all.

sentences.zh: 在中書省直，夜往鄰省，誤著履出閣，依事自列門下；

translations.literal: While on duty in the Secretariat, at night he went to a neighboring office, mistakenly wearing shoes out through the gate; according to regulation he reported himself to the Gate Office;
translations.idiomatic: While on duty in the secretariat he went one night to a neighboring office and mistakenly walked out through the gate wearing shoes. As regulations required, he reported himself to the gate office;

sentences.zh: 門下以闇夜人不知，不受列。

translations.literal: the Gate Office, because it was dark night and no one had seen, did not accept the report.
translations.idiomatic: but the gate office, saying that no one had seen him in the dark, refused to accept the report.

sentences.zh: 長之固遣送之，曰：「一生不侮闇室。

translations.literal: Changzhi firmly sent it in again, saying: 'In all my life I do not deceive even a dark room.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhi insisted on submitting it again, saying: "All my life I have never cheated even a dark room.

sentences.zh: 」前後所蒞官，皆有風政，為後人所思。

translations.literal: ' In every office he had held, before and after, he had exemplary governance, and later people remember him.
translations.idiomatic: " In every office he held, before and after, he governed with exemplary integrity, and later generations remember him.

sentences.zh: 宋世言善治者，咸稱之。

translations.literal: Among those of the Song age who speak of good governance, all praise him.
translations.idiomatic: Among those in the Song who spoke of good governance, all praised him.

sentences.zh: 子師門，原鄉令。

translations.literal: His son Shimen was Magistrate of Yuanxiang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shimen served as magistrate of Yuanxiang.

sentences.zh: 元嘉十二年，轉在臨海，並以簡約見稱。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia he was transferred to Linhai, and in both [posts] was praised for simplicity and frugality.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year of Yuanjia he was transferred to Linhai, and in both posts was praised for simplicity and frugality.

sentences.zh: 所得祿秩，悉散之親故，妻子常饑寒。

translations.literal: All salary and emoluments he received he gave away to relatives and friends; his wife and children were often hungry and cold.
translations.idiomatic: He gave away all his salary and emoluments to relatives and friends, while his wife and children often went hungry and cold.

sentences.zh: 人有勸其營田者，秉之正色曰：「食祿之家，豈可與農人競利！

translations.literal: When someone urged him to cultivate fields, Bingzhi said with stern countenance: 'A household that lives on salary — how can it compete with farmers for profit!
translations.idiomatic: When someone urged him to cultivate fields, Bingzhi said sternly: "A household that lives on official salary — how can it compete with farmers for profit!

sentences.zh: 」在郡作書案一枚，及去官，留以付庫。

translations.literal: ' In the commandery he had one writing desk made, and when he left office he left it behind in the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: " In the commandery he had one writing desk made, and when he left office he left it in the government storehouse.

sentences.zh: 十七年，卒，時年六十。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he died, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he died at the age of sixty.

sentences.zh: 子徽，尚書都官郎，吳令。

translations.literal: His son Hui was Gentleman of the Ministry of Justice and magistrate of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: His son Hui served as a gentleman of the ministry of justice and as magistrate of Wu.

sentences.zh: 元兇殺徐湛之，徽以黨與見誅。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Evil killed Xu Fanzhi, Hui was executed as a partisan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Evil murdered Xu Fanzhi, Hui was executed as an accomplice.

sentences.zh: 子謐，昇明末為尚書吏部郎。

translations.literal: His son Mi in the last years of the Sheng era was Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mi served in the final years of the Sheng era as a gentleman of the ministry of personnel.

sentences.zh: 元嘉初，太祖遣大使巡行四方，兼散騎常侍孔默之、王歆之等上言：「宣威將軍、陳、南頓二郡太守李元德，清勤均平，姦盜止息。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanjia, the Founding Emperor sent great envoys to tour the four directions, and Concurrent Regular Cavalier Attendant Kong Mozhi, Wang Xinzhi, and others memorialized: 'General Who Proclaims Might, Prefect of Chen and Nandun commanderies Li Yuande is pure, diligent, even, and fair; treachery and theft have ceased.'
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yuanjia, Taizu sent grand envoys to tour the realm. Concurrent regular cavalier attendant Kong Mozhi, Wang Xinzhi, and others reported: "General Who Proclaims Might, prefect of Chen and Nandun, Li Yuande, is diligent, fair, and incorrupt; crime and theft have ceased."

sentences.zh: 彭城內史魏恭子，廉恪脩慎，在公忘私，安約守儉，久而彌固。

translations.literal: Pengcheng Interior Minister Wei Gongzi is scrupulous, cautious, and self-restrained; in public service he forgets private interest, keeps to simplicity and frugality, and over time becomes ever firmer.
translations.idiomatic: Pengcheng interior minister Wei Gongzi is scrupulous and self-restrained, forgets private interest in public duty, and holds to simplicity and frugality with growing firmness over the years.

sentences.zh: 前宋縣令成浦，治政寬濟，遺詠在民。

translations.literal: Former magistrate of Song county Cheng Pu governed with lenience and relief; his lingering praise remains among the people.
translations.idiomatic: Former magistrate of Song county Cheng Pu governed with lenience and relief, and the people still sing his praise.

sentences.zh: 前鮦陽令李熙國，在事有方，民思其政。

translations.literal: Former magistrate of Ziyang Li Xiguo in office had method; the people remember his governance.
translations.idiomatic: Former magistrate of Ziyang Li Xiguo handled affairs with sound method, and the people still miss his rule.

sentences.zh: 山桑令何道，自少清廉，白首彌厲。

translations.literal: Shansang magistrate He Dao from youth has been pure and clean; white-haired, he is ever more strict.
translations.idiomatic: Shansang magistrate He Dao has been incorrupt since youth and grows stricter still in old age.

sentences.zh: 應加褒齎，以勸於後。

translations.literal: They should receive added commendation and reward to encourage those who come after.
translations.idiomatic: They should receive further rewards to encourage officials who follow.

sentences.zh: 」乃進元德號寧朔將軍，恭子賜絹五十匹，穀五百斛；

translations.literal: ' Thereupon Yuande's title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the North; Gongzi was granted fifty bolts of silk and five hundred hu of grain;
translations.idiomatic: " Yuande was promoted to General Who Pacifies the North; Gongzi was granted fifty bolts of silk and five hundred hu of grain;

sentences.zh: 浦、熙國、道各賜絹三十匹，穀二百斛。

translations.literal: Pu, Xiguo, and Dao each were granted thirty bolts of silk and two hundred hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Pu, Xiguo, and Dao each received thirty bolts of silk and two hundred hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 王歆之，字叔道，河東人也。

translations.literal: Wang Xinzhi, styled Shudao, was a man of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xinzhi, courtesy name Shudao, came from Hedong.

sentences.zh: 曾祖愆期，有名晉世，官至南蠻校尉。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Qianqi was famous in the Jin age and reached office as Colonel of the Southern Man.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Qianqi was renowned in Jin times and rose to colonel of the southern Man.

sentences.zh: 祖尋之，光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xunzhi was Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xunzhi was grand master of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 父肇之，豫章公相。

translations.literal: His father Zhaozhi was chief minister to the Duke of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhaozhi was chief minister to the Duke of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 歆之被遇於太祖，歷顯官左民尚書，光祿大夫，卒官。

translations.literal: Xinzhi received favor from the Founding Emperor, passed through eminent offices as Minister of the Left for the People and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Xinzhi won favor under Taizu, rose through high office to minister of the left for the people and grand master of splendid happiness, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 元嘉九年，豫州刺史長沙王義欣上言：「所統威遠將軍、北譙梁二郡太守關中侯申季歷，自奉職邦畿，於茲五年，信惠並宣，威化兼著，外清姦暴，內輯民黎，役賦均平，閭井齊肅，綏穆初附，招攜荒遠，郊境之外，仰澤懷風，爵賞之授，績能是顯，宜升階秩，以崇獎勸。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yuanjia, Inspector of Yu Province the Prince of Changsha Yixin memorialized: 'Under my command General Who Distant Might, Prefect of Beiqiao and Liang commanderies Marquis of Guanzhong Shen Jili, since taking office in the capital region, for five years now, trust and kindness have both been proclaimed, authority and transformation jointly manifest; outwardly he has cleared treachery and violence, inwardly he has ordered the common people; corvée and taxes are even, lanes and wells are uniformly orderly; he has soothed the newly attached and drawn in the distant wilds; beyond the border districts they look up to his grace and cherish his influence; in granting ranks and rewards, merit and ability are what show—he should be raised in rank to honor and encourage.'
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of Yuanjia, Yu inspector the Prince of Changsha, Yixin, reported: "Under my command, General Who Distant Might, prefect of Beiqiao and Liang, Marquis of Guanzhong Shen Jili has served in the capital region for five years. Trust and kindness spread together, and his authority and civilizing influence are both evident. He has cleared violence abroad and ordered the people within; corvée and taxes are fair, and neighborhoods are orderly. He has soothed the newly submitted and won over the distant frontier. Beyond the borders men look up to his grace. His merit plainly deserves rank and reward, and his grade should be raised to encourage others."

sentences.zh: 」進號寧朔將軍。

translations.literal: ' His title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: " He was promoted to General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 其後晉壽太守郭啟玄亦有清節，卒官。

translations.literal: After this, Jinshou prefect Guo Qixuan also had a pure integrity and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Jinshou prefect Guo Qixuan likewise maintained a spotless record and died in office.
