sentences.zh: 元嘉二十八年，詔曰：「故綏遠將軍、晉壽太守郭啟玄往銜命虜庭，秉意不屈，受任白水，盡勤靡懈，公奉私餼，纖毫弗納，布衣蔬食，飭躬惟儉。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year of Yuanjia an edict said: 'The late General Who Soothes the Distance, Jinshou prefect Guo Qixuan formerly bore orders in the barbarian court, held his intent unbending, received appointment at Baishui, exhausted diligence without slackening, public service and private gifts—not a thread accepted, plain cloth and vegetable food, disciplining the person only in frugality.'
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year of Yuanjia an edict said: "The late General Who Soothes the Distance, Jinshou prefect Guo Qixuan, once carried orders into the barbarian court and would not bend his principles. Assigned to Baishui, he served tirelessly, accepted no private gifts whatsoever, wore plain cloth and ate simple food, and disciplined himself in frugality."

sentences.zh: 故超授顯邦，以甄廉績。

translations.literal: Therefore he was exceptionally appointed to a prominent commandery to distinguish his clean achievements.
translations.idiomatic: For this he was specially appointed to a prominent commandery to honor his clean record.

sentences.zh: 而介誠苦節，終始匪貳，身死之日，妻子凍餒，志操殊俗，良可哀悼。

translations.literal: Yet his upright sincerity and bitter integrity, from beginning to end not twofold—on the day his body died, wife and children were frozen and hungry; his will and conduct were unlike the common run, truly worthy of mourning.
translations.idiomatic: His upright sincerity and stern integrity never wavered from first to last. When he died, his wife and children were left cold and hungry. Conduct so unlike the common run is truly worthy of mourning.

sentences.zh: 可賜其家穀五百斛。」

translations.literal: Let his household be granted five hundred hu of grain.'
translations.idiomatic: Let his household be granted five hundred hu of grain."

sentences.zh: 時有北地傅僧祐、潁川陳瑉、高平張祐，並以吏才見知。

translations.literal: At the time there were Fu Sengyou of Beidi, Chen Min of Yingchuan, and Zhang You of Gaoping, all known for talent in administration.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Fu Sengyou of Beidi, Chen Min of Yingchuan, and Zhang You of Gaoping were all recognized for administrative talent.

sentences.zh: 僧祐事在《臧燾傳》。

translations.literal: Sengyou's affairs are in the biography of Zang Can.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyou is treated in the biography of Zang Can.

sentences.zh: 瑉為吳令，善發姦伏，境內以為神明。

translations.literal: Min was magistrate of Wu, skilled at exposing hidden wrongdoing; within the commandery he was regarded as a spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Min served as magistrate of Wu and excelled at exposing hidden crimes; the commandery regarded him as almost supernatural.

sentences.zh: 祐祖父湛，晉孝武世，以才學為中書侍郎，光祿勳。

translations.literal: You's grandfather Zhan, in the age of Jin Emperor Xiaowu, by talent and learning was Secretariat Gentleman and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: You's grandfather Zhan, in the reign of Jin Emperor Xiaowu, rose by learning to secretariat gentleman and grand master for splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 祐歷臨安、武康、錢塘令，並著能名，宋世言長吏者，以三人為首。

translations.literal: You successively held the magistracies of Lin'an, Wukang, and Qiantang, all with noted reputations for ability; when the Song age spoke of chief local officials, these three men headed the list.
translations.idiomatic: You served in turn as magistrate of Lin'an, Wukang, and Qiantang, winning a name for competence in each. When Song officials spoke of outstanding local administrators, these three headed the list.

sentences.zh: 元嘉中，高平太守潘詞，有清節。

translations.literal: During Yuanjia, Gaoping prefect Pan Ci had a pure integrity.
translations.idiomatic: During Yuanjia, Gaoping prefect Pan Ci maintained a spotless record.

sentences.zh: 子亮為昌慮令，亦著廉名，大明中，為徐州刺史劉道隆所表。

translations.literal: His son Liang was magistrate of Changlu and also had a noted reputation for integrity; in the Daming era he was memorialized by Xu Province Inspector Liu Daolong.
translations.idiomatic: His son Liang was magistrate of Changlu and likewise won a name for integrity; in the Daming era he was recommended by Xu inspector Liu Daolong.

sentences.zh: 世祖世，吳郡陸法真歷官有清節，嘗為劉秀之安北錄事參軍。

translations.literal: In the age of Emperor Shizu, Lu Fazhen of Wu commandery in successive offices had a pure integrity and once served as Recorder Aide to Liu Xiuzhi as Northern Pacification General.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Shizu, Lu Fazhen of Wu commandery held a series of offices with a clean reputation and once served as recorder aide to Liu Xiuzhi, northern pacification general.

sentences.zh: 泰山羊希與安北諮議參軍孫詵書曰：「足下同僚似有陸錄事者，此生東南名地，又張玄外孫，持身至清，雅有志節。

translations.literal: Taishan Yang Xi wrote to Northern Pacification Advisory Aide Sun Shen: 'Among your colleagues below there seems to be Recorder Lu: this man is from a famous place in the southeast, also a grandson by a daughter of Zhang Xuan, holds himself utterly pure, and elegantly has will and integrity.'
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xi of Taishan wrote to northern pacification advisory aide Sun Shen: "Among your colleagues there seems to be Recorder Lu. He comes from a distinguished southeastern family and is a grandson of Zhang Xuan. He conducts himself with exceptional purity and has genuine integrity."

sentences.zh: 年高官下，秉操不衰，計當日夕相與申意。

translations.literal: Advanced in years but low in rank, he holds his conduct undiminished; I reckon that before long you will together express your regard.
translations.idiomatic: Though advanced in years he still holds a modest post without letting his conduct fade. I expect you will soon make your regard for him known.

sentences.zh: 」太宗初，為南海太守，卒官。

translations.literal: ' At the beginning of Emperor Taizong's reign he was made prefect of Nanhai and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: " Early in Taizong's reign he became prefect of Nanhai and died in office.

sentences.zh: 太宗世，琅邪王悅，亦蒞官清正見知。

translations.literal: In the age of Emperor Taizong, Wang Yue of Langye also, in presiding over office, was known for pure uprightness.
translations.idiomatic: In Taizong's era Wang Yue of Langye was likewise known for governing with pure integrity.

sentences.zh: 悅字少明，晉右將軍羲之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Yue's style name was Shaoming; he was a great-great-grandson of Jin General of the Right Xizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yue, courtesy name Shaoming, was a great-great-grandson of Jin general of the right Wang Xizhi.

sentences.zh: 父靖之，官至司徒左長史。

translations.literal: His father Jingzhi reached office as Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jingzhi rose to left chief clerk under the minister of education.

sentences.zh: 靖之為劉穆之所厚，就穆之求侍中，如此非一。

translations.literal: Jingzhi was treated generously by Liu Muzhi and went to Muzhi to request the post of Palace Attendant—not once alone.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhi enjoyed Liu Muzhi's favor and repeatedly asked him for the post of palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 穆之曰：「卿若不求，久自得也。

translations.literal: Muzhi said: 'If you did not ask, in time you would obtain it on your own.'
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi said, "If you did not ask, you would have received it in time on your own."

sentences.zh: 」遂不果。

translations.literal: ' In the end it did not come to pass.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end he never received it.

sentences.zh: 悅泰始中，為黃門郎，御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the Taishi era Yue was Yellow Gate Gentleman and Imperial Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: During Taishi, Yue served as yellow gate gentleman and imperial censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 上以其廉介，賜良田五頃。

translations.literal: The emperor because of his integrity granted him five qing of fine fields.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted him five qing of fine farmland for his integrity.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書吏部郎，侍中，在門下，盡其心力。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Ministry of Personnel, Palace Attendant; in the Gate Department he exhausted mind and strength.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to gentleman of the ministry of personnel and palace attendant, and in the gate department gave his full energy.

sentences.zh: 五年，卒官，追贈太常。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died in office; posthumously enfeoffed as Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he died in office and was posthumously made minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 初，悅為侍中，檢校御府、太官、太醫諸署，得姦巧甚多。

translations.literal: At first, when Yue was Palace Attendant, he inspected and checked the Imperial Storehouse, Grand Provisioner, Imperial Physician, and other offices, discovering many crafty abuses.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Yue was palace attendant, he inspected the imperial storehouse, grand provisioner, imperial physician, and other offices and uncovered many abuses.

sentences.zh: 及悅死，眾咸謂諸署詋詛之，上乃收典掌者十餘人，桎梏云送淮陰，密令渡瓜步江，投之中流。

translations.literal: When Yue died, the multitude all said the various offices had cursed him; the emperor then seized more than ten persons in charge, put them in cangue and fetters saying they were sent to Huaiyin, secretly ordered them ferried across the Guabu River, and cast them into midstream.
translations.idiomatic: When Yue died, many believed the offices had cursed him. The emperor then arrested more than ten officials in charge, shackled them as if sending them to Huaiyin, secretly had them ferried across the Guabu River, and cast them into midstream.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：夫善政之於民，猶良工之於埴也，用功寡而成器多。

translations.literal: The historian remarks: Good government toward the people is like a skilled craftsman toward clay: little effort applied, yet many vessels formed.
translations.idiomatic: The historian remarks: Good government toward the people is like a skilled potter with clay: little effort yields many vessels.

sentences.zh: 漢世戶口殷盛，刑務簡闊，郡縣治民，無所橫擾，勸賞威刑，事多專斷，尺一詔書，希經邦邑，龔、黃之化，易以有成。

translations.literal: In the Han age households were abundant and flourishing, penal affairs were simple and broad; commanderies and counties governed the people without arbitrary disturbance; encouragement, rewards, authority, and punishments—affairs were largely decided on the spot; the foot-long edict rarely passed through the realm's towns; the transformations of Gong and Huang were easy to achieve.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times the population was abundant, penal matters were simple, and counties governed without arbitrary interference. Rewards and punishments were often decided on the spot, imperial edicts rarely reached local towns, and the civilizing models of Gong Yu and Huang Ba were easy to realize.

sentences.zh: 降及晚代，情偽繁起，民減昔時，務多前世，立績垂風，艱易百倍。

translations.literal: Descending to later ages, falsity and artifice arose in profusion; the people were fewer than in former times, affairs were more numerous than in earlier generations; to establish achievement and hand down influence was a hundred times harder.
translations.idiomatic: In later ages deceit multiplied, the population shrank, and official burdens grew. To leave a lasting achievement became a hundred times harder.

sentences.zh: 若以上古之化，治此世之民，今吏之良，撫前代之俗，則武城弦歌，將有未暇；

translations.literal: If with the transformation of highest antiquity one governed the people of this age, or if today's good officials soothed the customs of former generations, then the zither songs of Wucheng would have no leisure;
translations.idiomatic: If the civilizing ways of highest antiquity were applied to the people of this age, or if today's good officials had to govern the customs of earlier generations, then the zither-playing governance of Wucheng would find no leisure;

sentences.zh: 淮陽臥治，如或可勉。

translations.literal: the recumbent governance of Huaiyang might perhaps be barely attainable.
translations.idiomatic: only the recumbent governance of Huaiyang might barely be within reach.

sentences.zh: 未必今才陋古，蓋化有淳薄也。

translations.literal: It is not necessarily that today's talent is base compared with antiquity; it is rather that transformation has its pure and its thin.
translations.idiomatic: It is not that talent today is inferior to antiquity; rather, the moral climate has grown thinner.
